summary.headline: SAIL Q1 FY27 EBITDA rose over 50% to INR4,356 crore (16.7% margin) despite 4.8 Mt crude steel output, aided by advanced capital repairs and better NSR.
summary.overview: SAIL reported Q1 FY27 EBITDA of INR4,356 crore versus INR2,925 crore a year earlier, with margin of 16.7% and EBITDA per tonne of INR10,464. PBT and PAT rose to INR2,159 crore and INR1,636 crore from INR890 crore and INR685 crore. Crude steel output fell to 4.8 Mt (4.9 Mt CPLY) and sales volume dropped about 7-8% to 4.2 Mt, as major capital repairs at IISCO, Durgapur and Bokaro were advanced into Q1 by design. Average NSR was INR57,100/t, up about INR5,000/t from Q4 FY26, and borrowings were flat at INR21,729 crore versus INR21,663 crore at 1 March 2026.

segments.name: Iron ore / mines (third-party sales)
segments.commentary: Q1 iron ore sales turnover INR574 crore vs INR157 crore CPLY, with volume 1.1 Mt vs 0.31 Mt; EBITDA about INR150 crore. Sales are mainly from Odisha group of mines, and Chhattisgarh auctions have fructified for Q2.

segments.name: Product mix
segments.commentary: Flats about 52.7% and longs about 34.8% of sales; semis fell to about 11-12.5% from 14% in Q1 FY26. Finished steel share rose to 89% from 86%.

segments.name: NMDC Steel / RINL
segments.commentary: NMDC Steel marketing sales were nil vs 3.73 lakh t CPLY; RINL semis sales were about 93,000 t (new this year). NSL plus RINL combined was about 2.76 lakh t CPLY.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 volume guidance maintained, with growth over FY26 expected by year-end; Q2-Q4 production to exceed last year's levels.
Q2 NSR expected to be about INR1,000-2,000/t lower than Q1; July NSR averaged INR55,600/t (flats INR56,900, longs INR54,200).
Imported coking coal cost expected to fall about INR1,000-2,000/t from August; Q2 coal cost seen INR1,000-1,500/t below Q1 (Q1 imported INR21,300/t).
FY27 capex target INR15,000 crore, rising to over INR20,000 crore in FY28 and about INR25,000-26,000 crore thereafter.
Cost reduction of about INR2,000/t targeted in FY27 from Q2 onward; by FY29 variable cost down INR3,000-4,000/t from IISCO expansion, with fixed cost up INR1,500-2,000/t, net about INR2,000/t.
Inventory to be held flat in Q2 and reduced in Q3 and Q4 to lower FY27 inventory year-on-year.
Railway price revision for FY27 expected in FY28; management says no further downward hit to P&L expected.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex INR2,575 crore against Q1 target INR2,306 crore; full-year target INR15,000 crore.
Major capital repairs advanced into Q1 at IISCO, Durgapur and Bokaro, reducing crude steel output by about 0.1 Mt vs CPLY.
Durgapur: TMT bar mill planned to produce 0.8-0.9 Mt/yr, expected September to December 2027; this will sharply reduce semis availability from Durgapur.
Captive Tasra coking coal mine under development, production expected around December 2026; captive mine coal cost estimated INR5,000-6,000/t vs indigenous average INR13,100/t.
Subgrade iron ore fines inventory about 32 Mt; first auction of about 3 Mt put up, with rates awaited.
demand_pricing: Indian steel consumption grew more than 8% YoY in Q1 FY27 while production grew about 3%; net imports about 0.4-0.5 Mt vs about 0.3 Mt CPLY.
Gap between primary and secondary TMT narrowed to about INR5,000/t.
June to July long-product prices fell about INR2,000-3,000/t; recent upward momentum of INR500-1,000/t expected. Flat product prices fell about INR1,000/t between June and July.
Safeguard duty of 11.5% remains in place (second year of three-year term). Anti-dumping investigation has been initiated and may bring relief.
Government imposed definitive anti-dumping duty on met coke; management says no impact as SAIL has captive coke capacity matching its needs.
Coal mix: about 85% imported, 15% indigenous (of which about 5% from captive mines). Imported coking coal: hard about 62%, soft about 23%.
Rail price: provisional FY27 price about INR74,000/t, which management expects to be revised upward.

qa_highlights.question: What were Q1 NSR vs Q4, and how do July prices and Q2 NSR look?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 NSR was INR57,100/t vs Q4 INR52,000/t. Monsoon-driven seasonal decline expected in Q2, with Q2 NSR about INR1,000-2,000/t lower than Q1; longs more affected than flats.

qa_highlights.question: Is full-year volume guidance intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; management maintained full-year volume guidance and expects growth over last year by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for coal costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Imported coal was INR21,300/t in Q1 vs INR18,100/t in Q4. Index fell from about 235 to 220; coal cost expected to fall INR1,000-2,000/t from August.

qa_highlights.question: Is third-party iron ore sales growth sustainable, and what about subgrade inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Mines sales more than doubled YoY, adding about INR400 crore turnover and INR150 crore profit. Target of about 8 Mt for captive mines; subgrade inventory about 32 Mt with 3 Mt first auction in progress.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 capex and beyond?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 target INR15,000 crore; FY28 above INR20,000 crore; later years INR25,000-26,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost-reduction plan through FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR2,000/t cost cut in FY27 from Q2; by FY29 IISCO expansion cuts variable cost INR3,000-4,000/t, with fixed cost up INR1,500-2,000/t, net about INR2,000/t.

qa_highlights.question: How much did the Gulf conflict affect input costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Fuel impact limited due to in-plant gas use; flux cost up on freight but offset by lower usage, saving about INR25 crore. Limestone and imported coal costs rose; coal up about INR3,500/t YoY.

risks_watch: Q2 seasonal weakness: monsoon-driven NSR decline and rain-hit demand; management aims to hold inventory flat in Q2.
Logistics constraints (rake availability) still limit mine sales; subgrade auction outcome pending.
Pay commission from 1 January 2027; wage provision decision deferred to Q4 FY27.
Railway price revision (FY27 price to be set in FY28) and anti-dumping outcome on flats.
Working capital borrowings reduction and inventory reduction in Q3-Q4 to meet deleveraging goal.
Production volume recovery in Q2-Q4 after Q1 maintenance; Tasra captive coal timing (around December 2026).
summary.management_tone: Confident on profitability and cost trajectory, with the margin and per-tonne EBITDA framed as best-in-years. Cautious and hedged on Q2 pricing and volume, with many figures described as guesswork and some answers unclear or deflected.
key_quotes: EBITDA margin at 16.7% is one of the best since '21 -'22, when the steel market at that time was at its peak and coal price was at its bottom in '21 -'22.
EBITDA per tonne also crossed a benchmark figure of INR10,000 per tonne and stood at INR10,464 per tonne in quarter 1 '26 -'27.
Yes, we are maintaining the full year volume, and we'll be having a growth over last year by the year-end.
So far as capex is concerned, this year, we're planning a target of INR15,000 crores, and this is going to increase in the next 2, 3 years because our expanses are on.

adds.what: Captive Tasra coking coal mine (feeds raw material, not steel capacity)

growth.why: FY27 volume guided to grow over FY26 by year-end and capex of INR15,000 crore (rising to over INR20,000 crore in FY28), with growth backed by the IISCO expansion, Durgapur TMT mill (Sep-Dec 2027) and an iron ore third-party sales target of 8 Mt, though no specific order or capacity-volume bridge was quantified; Q1 volumes fell about 7-8% YoY and crude output dipped to 4.8 Mt.
